decision_point: Specified after measuring lossless serialization of the Gemma manifest, before opening any graded outcomes from the 15 fresh editor runs. Execution statuses and some usage were available. This comparison is separate from the original three-arm protocol.
scope: Use exactly the same five official task IDs, same model, medium reasoning, 5-turn limit, 1536 output tokens per response and $6.50 cap per trajectory as live-design.json. Run all five grouped trajectories or none. No selection of tasks or repetition based on outcomes.
treatment: The grouped arm provides all 445 writable names and shapes at the opening using a reversible representation of consecutive equal-layout transformer layers, plus its short decoding instruction. Use the same public metadata preparation, on-demand read tool, SAE policy, public feedback and submission semantics as the paged and eager arms. The source ordered list must round-trip exactly.
primary_comparison: Grouped versus paged total provider editor tokens by task and pooled across all attempts. Report total, cached and uncached input, output, submissions, grade, target/controls preservation and equal-turn-prefix traffic. Native and eager remain external and flat-list references respectively.
gate: Wait for terminal editor records and conservative charges for all 15 original attempts. Launch the five additional attempts only when $32.50 remains under the same $100 combined authorized API ceiling. Each of the five has its own $6.50 hard cap. No semantic-judge API calls.
order: Run grouped after the original three arms, in the original prespecified family order. Record this timing difference when interpreting caches and later samples.
limitations: One trajectory per condition per task, five deterministic-grader families, no quality-equivalence claim and no additional test tasks. A competitive score/tokens result against this full-information control is necessary to credit paging beyond compact representation.
